intro: Three relative words that don't point back to a specific noun. wer (whoever, anyone who) opens a generalising relative clause that is the subject or object of the main clause: Wer gut schläft, (der) lernt besser; Wem du hilfst, der dankt dir — the demonstrative der / den / dem in the main clause is optional when the cases match (wer … der) and required when they don't (wem … der). was (which, what) refers to a whole clause (Er hat bestanden, was mich freute), to indefinite pronouns (alles, nichts, etwas, vieles, das) and to superlatives used as nouns (das Beste, was …), and stands alone in das, was (that which). wo / wohin / woher replace in der / zu dem / aus dem for places (die Stadt, wo ich geboren bin) and are the only option for city and country names (Berlin, wo …). These are the relatives that trip learners up — 'alles, ___ er sagt' — and the wer-sentence is the natural way to make a general point (Wer rastet, der rostet).
tips[0].title: wer …, (der) … — the generalising relative
tips[0].text: Wer gut schläft, lernt besser (= jeder, der …). Wer kommen will, ist willkommen. Wem du hilfst, der dankt dir (dative in the wer-clause, nominative in the main clause → der is required). Wen ich mag, den lade ich ein.
tips[0].trap: English 'whoever' is one word for all cases; German declines: wer (Nom), wen (Akk), wem (Dat), wessen (Gen), and the echo der / den / dem in the main clause changes with it.
tips[0].check.why: vertrauen takes the dative, so the generalising relative is wem; the main clause echoes it with dem.
tips[1].title: was after alles / nichts / etwas / das / superlatives, and for a whole clause
tips[1].text: alles, was er sagt · nichts, was ich weiß · etwas, was mich stört · das, was du meinst · das Beste, was ich gehört habe · Er hat bestanden, was mich freut (the whole fact pleases me). With a preposition: wo(r)-: etwas, worauf ich warte; das, wovon ich träume.
tips[1].check.why: The relative refers to the whole previous clause (the fact that he apologised), so it must be was.
tips[1].visual.rows[1].b: das Beste, was ich je gegessen habe
tips[1].visual.rows[2].b: Er kam zu spät, was mich ärgerte.
tips[2].title: wo / wohin / woher for places
tips[2].text: die Stadt, wo ich geboren bin (= in der) · der Ort, wohin wir fahren (= zu dem) · das Land, woher ich komme (= aus dem) · Berlin, wo ich wohne (names take only wo). wo is also used for a time: der Tag, wo … (colloquial; better: an dem).
tips[2].check.why: Origin (aus dem) is woher; wohin is direction towards, wo is location.
tips[3].title: was = 'which' for a thing that has no noun
tips[3].text: If the antecedent is a whole sentence, a pronoun (alles, nichts, etwas, das) or a superlative noun (das Schönste), it's was. If it's a real noun (der Film), it's der/die/das.
tips[3].check.why: The antecedent is a real noun (der Roman), so you use der/die/das, here accusative den; was is only for clauses, pronouns and superlatives.
remember[0]: wer … (der): anyone who; wem/wen in the clause, der/den echo in the main clause.
remember[1]: alles / nichts / etwas / das / superlative + was; whole clause + , was; place + wo / wohin / woher.
mistakes[0].why: After alles the relative is was.
mistakes[1].why: Cases differ (wem / der) → the echo pronoun is required.
hook: Make general points like Wer rastet, der rostet, and stop saying alles, das when German wants alles, was.
